THE ROLE
We are seeking a talented and motivated Graduate Analog Design Engineer to join our team and contribute to the design of high-performance serial links and data converters for our chiplet solutions. • Modelling & Scripting: Build behavioural models (e.g. Verilog-A) and scripts (e.g. Python, SKILL or OCEAN) to speed up simulation, analysis and design-check flows.

• Silicon Characterization Support: Help prepare test plans and support lab characterisation and debug of silicon as projects progress.

• Design Documentation: Document your designs, simulation results and design-review material clearly, supporting efficient knowledge sharing within the team.

• Technology Awareness: Keep learning about advances in high-speed SerDes, data converters and chiplet interfaces such as UCIe.

title: CENTRALE LYON - Post Doctoral Open and Flexible System-Level Evaluation Framework for Emerging AI Computing Architectures

description: Emerging computing technologies - non-volatile and ferroelectric memories, analog and digital in-memory computing, silicon photonics, 3D integration, and heterogeneous chiplets - offer major gains in energy efficiency, latency, bandwidth, and functionality. Their potential cannot, however, be established from device or circuit results alone: it requires a rigorous link between technology characteristics, architectural choices, workload mapping, and application-level figures of merit. The Electronics group at the Lyon Institute of Nanotechnology (INL) is seeking a (m/f) postdoctoral researcher to develop an open, modular and extensible system-level evaluation framework for design space exploration (DSE) and system-design-technology co-optimization (SDTCO) of emerging computing architectures. The focus is at the interface of computer architecture, accelerator design, performance modelling and hardware-software codesign, while making systematic use of lower-level device, circuit and array results so that architectural conclusions remain physically credible. The objective is to convert low-level results - compact models, measured or simulated KPIs, variability and reliability constraints, and multi-objective Pareto fronts - into parameterized architectural models supporting efficient exploration of accelerators for emerging AI workloads. The framework must enable both bottom-up projection, from device/circuit/array choices toward system performance, and top-down constraint propagation, from targets for energy, latency, throughput, accuracy, robustness and area toward technology and circuit requirements. It will consolidate ongoing INL activities in predictive system assessment, DTCO, emerging memories, compute-in-memory and photonic computing, integrating or extending existing components with emphasis on openness, reproducibility and reusability. <p

description:
Role Title: Optomechanical Design Engineer - Precision CNC Parts (Remote)
Role Type: Contractor
Location: Fully remote
Opportunity Snapshot
Pay: $90 -$155/hour
Duration: Initial phase of 20 part packages; production phase to follow
Location: Fully remote, no geographic restrictions
You'll need: 5+ years designing CNC-machined production parts, technical decision authority, and access to parametric CAD software
Your tasks: Author original CAD part packages, and peer review packages from other engineers
micro1 is engaging senior optomechanical and mechanical design engineers to create original CAD part packages for a client project in precision optics and optomechanics. Your engineering judgment is what matters here - no prior AI experience required.
Each package is a new part you design from scratch: a difficult, high-value CNC part with a specific machining challenge, backed by a drawing with full GD&T, a design rationale, and a production scenario you justify from experience. Every part is independently reviewed by three other engineers, and you'll review others' work as well.
What you'll do

• Design original parts in parametric CAD, delivered as native files plus STEP.

• Produce the technical drawing: dimensions, tolerances, GD&T and datums, material and condition, finish, revision, drawing standard.

• Write the design context: intended function, interfaces, operating conditions, the machining challenge, and your material and process rationale.

• Build the production scenario: estimated unit cost and drivers, CNC cycle and setup hours, assumed volume, sourcing difficulty and lead time - with the engineering basis for each estimate.

• Peer review other engineers' packages against technical quality, production realism, and engineering value, with part-specific evidence for every score.

• Revise your own packages against review findings.

What we're looking for

• 5+ years of production engineering experience with comparable CNC parts, materials and processes in precision optics or optomechanics.

•
Technical decision authority: you owned or approved critical design choices - drawing, tolerance or material approval, production release, or enforcing engineering quality standards. Design leads, principal and staff engineers, and technical authorities are the profile.

• Experience at OEMs or specialist suppliers whose engineering standards you can reproduce.

• Strong GD&T and tolerancing judgment, including cost and inspection implications.

• Access to parametric CAD software (SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, Creo or similar) and the ability to deliver native files plus STEP.

• Industry experience, not academic.

Important: originality and IP
Every design must be your own original work. You cannot use designs owned by a current or former employer or customer, and you cannot substitute public or purchased CAD. All deliverables become the client's property. If you're currently employed, check your employment agreement regarding outside work and invention assignment before applying.

• Apply and complete the screening questions

• Complete the AI interview for this role - it's how your expertise gets in front of the client

• Profile review, including evidence of comparable parts and decisions owned
